This composite page covers **Region Syddanmark** and **Syddanmark**, two closely related but distinct entities within the context of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (Acute Surgery Database). **Region Syddanmark** refers specifically to the regional health authority and administrative organization responsible for healthcare delivery and data reporting. In contrast, **Syddanmark** denotes the broader geographical and statistical region within [[danmark|Danmark]], used to aggregate and compare hospital-level outcomes and patient demographics. Disambiguating these two is essential: one is the administrative body that interacts with national databases, while the other is the geographic container for clinical data.

The connection between these two entities is critical for understanding regional healthcare performance in Denmark. As an organization, Region Syddanmark actively engages with the database, such as by providing official comments on the 2023 annual report [^src2]. Geographically and statistically, Syddanmark encompasses several major hospitals, including [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]], [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]], [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]], and [[sygehus-soenderjylland|Sygehus Sønderjylland]] [^src11]. 

When analyzing clinical quality indicators, the region frequently records some of the lowest national performance rates, highlighting significant areas for systemic improvement. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] (administration of antibiotics within three hours of hospital arrival), the region's performance was notably low. During the period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023, Syddanmark recorded a compliance rate of just 13.5% (95% CI: 10.6–16.9) [^src8]. This improved slightly but remained the lowest nationally in the subsequent period from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024, reaching 22.5% (95% CI: 19.2–26.0) [^src13], compared to 44.6% in [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] [^src3]. 

Region Syddanmark also shows distinct results for other clinical indicators. For [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] (intermediate admission), the rate varied regionally, reaching 27.0% in Region Syddanmark [^src4]. For a supplementary indicator ([[indikator-5x|supplerende-indikator-5x]]), 17.8% of patients in the region were operated on within 6 hours for perforation, ischemia, or bleeding [^src9]. Furthermore, the region had the lowest regional fulfillment for [[indikator-8|indikator-8-ernaering]] at just 0.2% [^src10], and for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], the rate varied up to 56.8% in the region [^src14]. In terms of mortality, 9.9% of patients in Syddanmark with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]] died within 30 days after acute surgery [^src11]. 

Despite these variations in clinical outcomes and process indicators, demographic and baseline health comparisons show consistency across the country. The [[asa-score|ASA]] score for operated patients is not significantly different across regions, including [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], and Syddanmark [^src6]. Similarly, there is no significant difference in patient [[alder|alder]] across the regions [^src12]. Ultimately, this composite page demonstrates how the administrative authority and its corresponding statistical geography are both integral to evaluating acute surgical care, tracking hospital-level data, and identifying regional disparities in the Danish healthcare system.
